text.p: These are the headlines selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pearson pledge could cost $1 billion: Cancellation of airport plan means Ottawa will take in millions less, documents suggest.
- Leaders put futures on the line on the air: TV debates vital to election image.
- Thousands of Turks protest secularism: Huge rally asks military to let country's Islamic schools stay open.
- Machine truimphs over man: IBM's Deep Blue wins chess match.
- Columnist faces hate charges: B.C. freedom-of-speech case finds unlikely allies.
- India, Pakistan hoping to end feud: Disputed Kashmir remains big sticking points as new Prime Ministers meet in effort to undo 50 years of bitterness, strengthen economic ties.
- APEC takes on key trade role: Asia-Pacific nations agree to move quickly to open markets in up to 15 economic sectors.
- Investment dealers bank on top-ranked analysts: The financial community closely watches Brendan Wood's annual survey of institutional investors to find out where the stars are.
- Cash-short union faces staff cuts: CEP says survival not at risk.
- Big shakeup at Molson: Molson family overhauls board, replaces recently appointed CEO Norm Seagram with Montreal lawyer James Arnett and looks to fast-track return to brewing roots.
